correctness.rationale: A rotation with three 1 symbols is unbordered iff its first and last letters differ. For v=1 0^a 1 0^b 1 0^c, a direct border argument proves unbordered iff a<c, with the reversed companion lemma. Each inequality of cyclic consecutive zero gaps gives precisely one unbordered rotation, yielding U(w)=[a!=b]+[b!=c]+[c!=a] in {0,2,3}. Counting nonnegative gap triples summing n-3: one all-equal if 3|n and 3(floor((n-3)/2)+1-[3|n]) triples with exactly two equal. Marking one of three occurrences of 1 gives n/3 cyclic positions per gap triple, yielding C0=n[3|n]/3, C2=n(floor((n-3)/2)+1-[3|n]) and C3=binom(n,3)-C0-C2. Handles periodic all-equal and n=3. Independently enumerated direct proper-border tests on all 2380 three-one strings for n=3,...,16 and checked every formula; all-length proof is combinatorial, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The first binary sparse weight where a third unbordered rotation is possible admits a sharp, nontrivial trichotomy and explicit all-n counts. A natural restricted joint histogram can be useful for word-conjugacy enumeration even if the proof is elementary; it is not an arbitrary single-length slice or known table replay.

limitations: Binary alphabet, exactly 3 ones, n>=3, indexed rotations rather than rotation equivalence or complement classes.
